# Getting started (/docs/getting-started)

Mandate lets an AI agent spend money only within rules a person signed, and lets anyone check afterwards that it did.
This API is for the other side of the payment: **a seller, marketplace or auditor checking an agent's payment before shipping**.

## Check an agent payment in one call [#check-an-agent-payment-in-one-call]

You need only the PayPal order id the payment arrived with. No account and no key: everything is checked with Mandate's public keys.

```bash
curl https://mandate-e13m.onrender.com/api/verify/{paypalOrderId}
```

The answer says whether:

- the buyer **signed a mandate** that allows this purchase (an AP2 Intent Mandate),
- the cart is the **exact cart** the merchant signed and the buyer's rules allowed,
- **PayPal's own record** shows that amount captured,
- and, if the buyer approved it, that **their device signed** that cart (a passkey).

## With the SDK [#with-the-sdk]

```ts
import { MandateApiClient, ServerEnvironment } from "mandate-api";

const client = new MandateApiClient({ serverEnvironment: ServerEnvironment.Production });
const verdict = await client.verification.verifyOrder({ paypalOrderId: "5O190127TN364715T" });
if (!verdict.ok) throw new Error("Don't ship: this payment isn't backed by the buyer's mandate");
```

SDKs are generated by APIMatic for **TypeScript**, **Python** and **C#**.

## Next [#next]

- [How Mandate decides](how-mandate-decides.md): the 7 rules every purchase goes through.
- The API reference, generated from Mandate's OpenAPI document.


# How Mandate decides (/docs/how-mandate-decides)

Every purchase an agent tries, whether from Mandate's own agent, a scheduled buy, or an outside assistant over MCP, goes through the same gate. It checks 7 rules in order:

| # | Rule | If it fails |
|---|------|-------------|
| 1 | **Mandate**: active, not expired, right currency | Blocked |
| 2 | **Request came from** the user's task, not text on a web page | Blocked |
| 3 | **Category** is one the user allowed | Blocked |
| 4 | **Seller** is verified and not on the user's blocked list | Blocked |
| 5 | **Item limit**: under the per-item cap | The user is asked |
| 6 | **Market price**: not too far above similar items (Channel3) | The user is asked |
| 7 | **Budget**: fits what is left this period | The user is asked |

Allowed purchases get a one-time permit for that exact cart and price; only then does Mandate use PayPal. Every decision is a signed, hash-chained receipt, and each one records how all 7 rules came out.

The gate is plain code, not a model: the same purchase always gets the same answer.


# Context Plugin (/docs/context-plugin)

The context plugin teaches your AI coding assistant how to use this API's SDKs, so the code it writes for you calls the API the way the SDKs are meant to be used.

## Install [#install]

```bash
npx context-plugins install "https://mandate-e13m.onrender.com/docs/__downloads/plugin.zip"
```

## What it does [#what-it-does]

Once the plugin is installed, describe what you want to build and your assistant works from the SDK for your language: how to install it and create a client, how to authenticate, and which methods and types to use for each call. You spend less time correcting code written from guesses about the API.

## Supported languages [#supported-languages]

- TypeScript
- Python
- C#

## Supported platforms [#supported-platforms]

- Claude Code
- Cursor
- GitHub Copilot

# C# SDK (/docs/sdks/csharp)

[Download SDK](/docs/__downloads/sdk/csharp.zip)

## Intro [#intro]

The Mandate API SDK provides access to the Mandate API REST APIs.

Mandate is an authorisation layer for AI-agent payments on PayPal. Every agent payment carries
AP2 v0.2 mandates (the customer's signed limits, the merchant's signed checkout, the agent's closed
mandates) and signed receipts. The **Verification** endpoints let a seller, PayPal or a dispute
reviewer check a payment with public keys alone. The **Demo** endpoints drive the same flow the app
uses: sign rules, let the agent shop, approve over-limit purchases.

Sandbox only. No real money moves. Without keys the server runs fully offline with simulated
PayPal order IDs (`SIM-…`); with PayPal sandbox keys the IDs are real sandbox order IDs.

## Installation [#installation]

Add the SDK as a project reference into your solution:

```bash
dotnet add reference <path-to-sdk>/src/MandateApi/MandateApi.csproj
```

The project takes its build settings from the files around it, so reference it in place.

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

### Dependency Injection [#dependency-injection]

Register the client with `IServiceCollection` and resolve it from the container. The `HttpClient` is managed by `IHttpClientFactory`. Configure the client's behavior through `MandateApiClientOptions`.

```csharp
services.AddMandateApiClient(options =>
{
    options.AutomationSecret = "YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN";
    options.Environment = ServerEnvironment.Production;
    // TODO: configure more client options here
});
```

### Direct Instantiation [#direct-instantiation]

Create the client by passing an `HttpClient` you manage yourself. Configure the client's behavior through `MandateApiClientOptions`.

```csharp
var httpClient = new HttpClient();
// TODO: configure more client options here
var options = new MandateApiClientOptions
{
    AutomationSecret = "YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN",
    Environment = ServerEnvironment.Production,
};
var client = new MandateApiClient(httpClient, options);
```

# Python SDK (/docs/sdks/python)

[Download SDK](/docs/__downloads/sdk/python.zip)

## Intro [#intro]

The Mandate API SDK provides access to the Mandate API REST APIs.

Mandate is an authorisation layer for AI-agent payments on PayPal. Every agent payment carries
AP2 v0.2 mandates (the customer's signed limits, the merchant's signed checkout, the agent's closed
mandates) and signed receipts. The **Verification** endpoints let a seller, PayPal or a dispute
reviewer check a payment with public keys alone. The **Demo** endpoints drive the same flow the app
uses: sign rules, let the agent shop, approve over-limit purchases.

Sandbox only. No real money moves. Without keys the server runs fully offline with simulated
PayPal order IDs (`SIM-…`); with PayPal sandbox keys the IDs are real sandbox order IDs.

## Installation [#installation]

Add the SDK to your project from its folder, with whichever package manager your project uses. Give each tool a path containing a slash, such as `../mandate-api` — a bare folder name is looked up on PyPI instead, and resolves to whatever project holds that name there:

```bash
pip install <path-to-sdk>
```

```bash
uv add <path-to-sdk>
```

```bash
poetry add <path-to-sdk>
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

### Synchronous client [#synchronous-client]

Construct `MandateApiClient` with keyword arguments, and call `close()` when you are done. Every argument is optional.

```python
from mandate_api import MandateApiClient

client = MandateApiClient(automation_secret="YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN", environment="production")

client.close()
```

Alternatively, scope it — `with MandateApiClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

### Asynchronous client [#asynchronous-client]

`AsyncMandateApiClient` mirrors `MandateApiClient` with **identical method names**, and every endpoint method is a coroutine. It takes the same arguments, with some differences — for example, the transport argument is `custom_async_http_client`.

```python
from asyncio import run

from mandate_api import AsyncMandateApiClient

async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncMandateApiClient(automation_secret="YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN", environment="production")
    await client.aclose()

run(main())
```

Alternatively, scope it — `async with AsyncMandateApiClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

# TypeScript SDK (/docs/sdks/typescript)

[Download SDK](/docs/__downloads/sdk/typescript.zip)

## Intro [#intro]

The Mandate API SDK provides access to the Mandate API REST APIs.

Mandate is an authorisation layer for AI-agent payments on PayPal. Every agent payment carries
AP2 v0.2 mandates (the customer's signed limits, the merchant's signed checkout, the agent's closed
mandates) and signed receipts. The **Verification** endpoints let a seller, PayPal or a dispute
reviewer check a payment with public keys alone. The **Demo** endpoints drive the same flow the app
uses: sign rules, let the agent shop, approve over-limit purchases.

Sandbox only. No real money moves. Without keys the server runs fully offline with simulated
PayPal order IDs (`SIM-…`); with PayPal sandbox keys the IDs are real sandbox order IDs.

## Installation [#installation]

The SDK compiles to `dist/` before it can be referenced — run its `build` script once in the SDK folder, then add it to your project by path:

```bash
npm install <path-to-sdk>
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

Create one client and reuse it. Configure its behaviour through `ClientOptions`.

```ts
import { MandateApiClient, ServerEnvironment } from "mandate-api";

const client = new MandateApiClient({
  serverEnvironment: ServerEnvironment.Production,
  automationSecret: "YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN",
});
```

Nothing in `ClientOptions` is required — `new MandateApiClient()` compiles — and each option left out falls back to its default. `serverEnvironment` is spelled out above so the environment a call reaches is visible where the client is built rather than inherited silently.

### From CommonJS [#from-commonjs]

The package ships both dialects from a single entry, so `require` works with full types. In a TypeScript CommonJS file use the `import ... = require(...)` form — a plain destructuring `require` runs fine but gives you `any`.

```ts
import sdk = require("mandate-api");

const client = new sdk.MandateApiClient({
  serverEnvironment: sdk.ServerEnvironment.Production,
  automationSecret: "YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN",
});
```

# Pause, resume or revoke spending from an automation (/docs/api/openapi/automation/killSwitch)

`POST /api/automation/kill-switch`

For a Zap such as "text STOP to pause every agent". Without `mandateId` it acts on all of the
user's mandates. Logged in the signed decision log as "via automation".


# Server status and which services are live or simulated (/docs/api/openapi/demo/getHealth)

`GET /api/health`

Which integrations this server is running with: real PayPal sandbox or simulated payments, the
model behind the agent, where data is stored, and whether Zapier alerts and the kill switch are on.
Always sandbox-only.


# The demo user's mandates (/docs/api/openapi/demo/listMandates)

`GET /api/mandates`

Every mandate the demo user has signed, with its rules and status (active, paused or revoked).

# Sign spending rules (/docs/api/openapi/demo/createMandate)

`POST /api/mandates`

With only `text`, the rules reader (the configured model, or the offline reader) turns the
sentence into a policy and Mandate signs it. With `policy`, the rules the user reviewed are
validated and signed. Rate limited when the model is called.


# Let the shopping agent carry out a task under a mandate (/docs/api/openapi/demo/runAgent)

`POST /api/agent/run`

The agent can only search, read and propose. Each proposal goes through the policy gate, which
pays, asks the user, or blocks. With `stream: true` the response is NDJSON, one step per line.


# Purchases waiting for the user (/docs/api/openapi/demo/listApprovals)

`GET /api/approvals`

Purchases the gate sent to the user (over a soft limit), with when each request expires.

# Approve or decline a purchase (/docs/api/openapi/demo/decideApproval)

`POST /api/approvals/{id}`

If the user has a passkey, approving needs a WebAuthn assertion over this exact cart
(challenge from `GET /api/approvals/{id}/passkey`). Hard rules (category, seller, injected
instructions) can never be approved through.


# Verdict for an agent payment (/docs/api/openapi/verification/verifyOrder)

`GET /api/verify/{paypalOrderId}`

Is this PayPal order backed by a mandate the buyer signed? Returns the Mandate v1 checks
(Intent, Cart and Payment Mandates, Ed25519), the `paypal_order_record` check (PayPal's own
order record, read with the PayPal Server SDK, shows the signed amount captured), and the
AP2 v0.2 verdict in `ap2`.
Fulfil only when `ok` and `ap2.ok` are both true.


# AP2 v0.2 evidence pack for a PayPal order (/docs/api/openapi/verification/getAp2Evidence)

`GET /api/ap2/orders/{paypalOrderId}`

The merchant-signed checkout JWT, the Checkout and Payment Mandate chains (SD-JWT, ES256),
the checkout and payment receipts, budget context, the passkey assertion if the buyer approved
on their device, and every check with its result. Verify independently with `/api/ap2/jwks`.


# A merchant's agent payments with their verdicts (/docs/api/openapi/verification/listSellerPayments)

`GET /api/seller`

Every agent payment to a merchant, newest first, each with its Mandate v1 verdict and AP2 v0.2
result. A seller's queue of "safe to fulfil" and "don't ship" orders.


# Verify a Mandate v1 credential chain you hold (/docs/api/openapi/verification/verifyChain)

`POST /api/verify`

Checks an Intent, Cart and Payment Mandate chain against the published keys.

# ES256 public keys (JWKS) for every AP2 credential (/docs/api/openapi/keys/getAp2Jwks)

`GET /api/ap2/jwks`

Provider, agent, payment gateway, merchants and users. Look keys up by `kid`.

# All public keys, Mandate v1 (Ed25519 PEM) and AP2 v0.2 (JWKS) (/docs/api/openapi/keys/getTrust)

`GET /api/trust`

The full trust bundle in one call: users' and merchants' Ed25519 keys (with each merchant's
verified status), the platform key, and the AP2 JWKS. Cache it to verify payments offline.


# Ed25519 public key that signs receipts and permits (/docs/api/openapi/keys/getReceiptPublicKey)

`GET /api/public-key`

The PEM public key for checking the `signature` on every receipt in the decision log.

# The signed, hash-chained decision log (/docs/api/openapi/receipts/listReceipts)

`GET /api/receipts`

Every decision Mandate made, in order. Each receipt carries the hash of the one before it and an
Ed25519 signature, so any edit, insertion or deletion breaks the chain.


# Verify the server's own log (/docs/api/openapi/receipts/verifyServerLog)

`GET /api/receipts/verify`

Re-checks every hash link and signature in the server's decision log.

# Verify a copy of the log you hold (/docs/api/openapi/receipts/verifyLogCopy)

`POST /api/receipts/verify`

Names the first altered entry (`brokenAt`) and why.
